t: You're looking at a bronze statue of Mahatma Gandhi in the middle of Tavistock Square, made by the Polish sculptor Fredda Brilliant. It was unveiled in 1968, marking the coming centenary of his birth in 1869. There's a local reason for it. Gandhi studied law at University College London, close by, from 1888 to 1891, before being called to the bar at the Inner Temple. He later led India's campaign for independence from British rule through nonviolent resistance, and his example inspired movements for freedom around the world.
